newsitem.title: USA: USDA trade adviser to EU to talk subsidies, other.
newsitem.headline: USDA trade adviser to EU to talk subsidies, other.

text.p: The senior trade adviser to Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman is going to Europe next week to meet with senior European Union officials on grain subsidies and other key agricultural issues.
USDA trade adviser Paul Drazek said Thursday that he will meet with officials in Brussels "to talk about a whole range of issues, including subsidies."
Drazek will then go to Geneva where he will observe the World Trade Organization's dispute settlement panel on the issue of Europe's controversial ban on U.S. meat treated with growth hormones.

Drazek said he wants to find out what the EU's current strategy is in subsidizing some recent sales of grain, and repeat the U.S. position that Washington is monitoring the situation closely and stands ready to use subsidies too if it is deemed necessary to maintain markets.
Drazek also said he will be discussing the current situation in Europe regarding gene-altered soybeans and corn.

The EU has approved genetically modified U.S. soybeans, but consumer groups have voiced concern about the product and called for labelling of the beans. Genetically engineered corn is awaiting a decision by the EU, and Secretary Glickman said the United States is watching the developments.
The issue of grain subsidies has flared up between the United States and European Union in recent weeks after EU restarted wheat subsidies in September.
Glickman has said USDA would fight to keep markets open for U.S. farmers, even if that means resorting to subsidies.
Drazek noted that although EU farm commissioner Franz Fischler commented earlier in the week that subsidies were not desirable, the EU subsidized another 300,000 tonnes of wheat shipments Thursday.
"The fact that they continue to do it is a concern," Drazek said. "Any time they subsidize in the world, we pay attention."
